title: ESPD XML mapping spec
description:
The declarative format of model/xml-mapping/*.mapping.json and model/parts/*/section*.mapping.json. A spec maps the instance data of the model (a JSON document, addressed by dotted paths) to a UBL ESPD Request or Response and back. One spec drives both directions: a rule is a correspondence between a path in the instance data and an element path in the XML, read left to right to write XML and right to left to read it. The format is a contract for implementations: an engine that runs these specs must support every construct below. (The reference engine is espd-demo/model/mapping-engine/mapper.mjs.)

Paths in the instance data are dotted (partIV.selectionCriteria.x.response.turnover). `[]` after a segment flattens across an array (a[].b). Paths into the XML are slash-separated element names with namespace prefixes (cac:TenderingCriterion/cbc:ID). An attribute value is a constant, a path into the instance data ({ from }) or a derived value ({ fromMap }). A leaf that has no value in the instance data produces no element.

target.description: The XML document the spec writes: the root element and the namespaces declared on it (an empty prefix is the default namespace).

rules.description: Applied in order. Every rule is exactly one of: a value rule, a forEach rule, a records rule, a structure rule (or a comment-only placeholder, which does nothing).

attributeValue.description: An XML attribute: a constant, a value from the instance data, or a value derived from another field.

anyOf.description: The value of an instance-data path; read back into that path on import.

Derived: the value of another field (path, relative to the current item) is looked up in a map; the default applies when there is no path or the value is not in the map. Written on export only, never read back. In a published spec the map is named, not spelled out: { profile } refers to a profile of registries/scheme-agency-profile.json, which an engine resolves into { map, default } before it runs the spec.
As the engine runs it, after the profile is resolved.

commentRule.description: A placeholder that carries only a comment; it does nothing.

valueRule.description: Write one value: the instance-data value at `from` (or the constant) becomes the text of the element at `to`, with `attributes`. Read back, the text of that element is written to `from`. A value that is absent, null or empty writes nothing. When both `from` and `const` are given, `from` wins if it has a value, otherwise the constant is written. Several rules may target the same element path; on import a constant attribute tells them apart.

when.description: Guard: the rule applies only when the instance-data value at `path` equals `equals`. On import the guard value is restored.

forEachRule.description: Repeat an element for every item of the array at `forEach`. The element is `to`; with `item.fields` each field is a value rule resolved against the item; with `item.path` the item is a scalar that goes into that child element; with neither, the scalar is the text of the element itself.

recordKey.description: The identifier element of a record. `to` is its path inside the record, `attributes` its scheme attributes. In the aggregate form `from` names the item field that is the key; in the scalar-item form `key` is the fixed identifier.

recordEntry.description: One record of a records rule: its key and exactly one body, a typed value, a nested object or cross-references to another record set.

object.description: The object at `from`; each field becomes a child element under the wrapper element `to`. Written only when at least one field has a value.

references.description: One cross-reference element (`to`, whose last segment holds the id) for the `key` of every item of the array at `forEach`. `resolve` rebuilds the items on import from the shared record set the ids point to.

recordsRule.description: Write a repeated record: a wrapper element (`records`) with a key and a body. Three forms. (1) `entries`: a fixed list of records, or with `forEach` the list is written once for every item of the array (and `childRecords` for arrays nested in the item). (2) `forEach` and `item.fields`: one record per item, all its fields inside it, with the key taken from `key.from`. (3) `forEach` and `item.path`: one record per scalar item, all with the fixed `key.key`, the item in the element `item.path`. `importVia: references` marks a record set that is rebuilt through references and not imported directly.

structureNode.description: A node of an embedded XML structure that mirrors the target XML one to one. `element` names it. It is a container (`children`), a constant leaf (`const`), a leaf bound to instance data (`from`, or `fromItem` inside a repeated element, where '.' is the item itself) or a repeated element (`forEach`, one element per array item). `valueMap` translates an instance value to the emitted text (for example true to a code). Sibling elements are always distinct nodes, so an element name can repeat. Only `from` and `fromItem` leaves, and `{ from }` attributes, are read back on import.

structureRule.description: An embedded XML structure written under the document root.
